front: Le verlan, c'est l'envers : on inverse les syllabes des mots.
pronunciation: [luh vehr-LAHN, seh lahn-VEHR : ohn nan-vehrs lay see-LAB day MOH]
back: Verlan is 'l'envers' backwards: you flip the syllables of words.
context: Verlan = l'envers (the reverse) reversed. Born in Paris suburbs, now everyday slang.
'Ouf' = verlan of 'fou' (crazy). Means amazing or crazy depending on tone.
'Chelou' = verlan of 'louche' (shady, weird).

front: Il est relou avec ses questions.
back: He's annoying with all his questions.
context: 'Relou' = verlan of 'lourd' (heavy, tiresome).
'Meuf' = verlan of 'femme' (woman, girlfriend). Very informal.

front: Il fait le beauf avec sa grosse voiture.
pronunciation: [eel feh luh BOHF ah-vek sah grohs vwah-TÜR]
back: He's acting all tacky with his big car.
context: 'Un beauf' (from 'beau-frère') = a vulgar, narrow-minded person.
'Béton' = verlan of 'tomber': 'laisse tomber' → 'laisse béton'. Made famous by a 1977 song by Renaud.

front: Il est vénère depuis ce matin.
back: He's been angry since this morning.
context: 'Vénère' = verlan of 'énervé' (angry).
'Un keum' = verlan of 'mec' (guy).
'Les keufs' = verlan of 'flics' (cops). Both are slang for 'la police'.
'Les rents-pa' = verlan of 'parents'. Very colloquial.
'La reum' = verlan of 'mère'. Like 'le reup' for 'père'.

front: Il s'est fait choper par le contrôleur.
pronunciation: [eel seh feh shoh-PAY par luh kohn-troh-LUHR]
back: He got caught by the ticket inspector.
context: 'Se faire choper' = to get caught (slang).
'Une clope' = a cigarette. 'T'as' = tu as.
'La thune' = money (slang). Also: le fric, le blé, l'oseille.
Shorter, informal version of 'coûter un bras et une jambe'.
'Se casser' = to leave (informal). Also 'se barrer', 'se tirer'.

front: Je me suis fait engueuler par le prof.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh swee feh tahn-guh-LAY par luh PROF]
back: I got told off by the teacher.
context: 'Se faire engueuler' = to get yelled at (informal).
'Un bouquin' = a book (informal).

back: I'm going to get some shut-eye.
context: 'Pioncer' = to sleep (slang). Also 'roupiller'.
'Cailler' = to be very cold (slang).

front: Il a bossé comme un malade.
context: 'Comme un malade' (like a sick person) = like crazy.
'Être à l'ouest' = to be spaced out, confused.

front: Il me prend la tête avec ses histoires.
pronunciation: [eel muh prahn lah TET ah-vek say zees-TWAHR]
back: He's doing my head in with his stories.
context: 'Prendre la tête' = to annoy, stress someone out. 'Une prise de tête' = a hassle.
'Mon délire' = my thing, my vibe (youth slang).
'Se prendre un râteau' (get hit by a rake) = to be rejected romantically.
'C'est réglé' = it's settled, sorted.

front: Je suis dégoûté, j'ai raté le concert.
pronunciation: [zhuh swee day-goo-TAY, zhay rah-tay luh kohn-SEHR]
back: I'm gutted, I missed the concert.
context: 'Dégoûté' in slang = gutted, disappointed (not disgusted).

back: That's so annoying! / What a bummer!
context: 'Avoir le seum' = to be bitter, frustrated (from Arabic 'samm', poison).
'Wesh' (from Algerian Arabic) = hey, yo. Very informal, youth and banlieue slang.

front: Il fait le malin devant ses potes.
pronunciation: [eel feh luh mah-LAN duh-vahn say POT]
back: He's showing off in front of his mates.
context: 'Faire le malin' = to show off. 'Un pote' = a mate.
'Une dinguerie' (from 'dingue') = something amazing or crazy. Recent youth slang.
'PLS' (position latérale de sécurité, the recovery position) = completely overwhelmed, humorously.
'Askip' = 'à ce qu'il paraît' (apparently), shortened in texting and speech.
'Gênant' = embarrassing, cringeworthy.

front: On s'est tapé un fou rire.
context: 'Un fou rire' = uncontrollable laughter. 'Se taper' = to have, treat oneself to (informal).

front: Elle a pécho le numéro du serveur.
pronunciation: [el ah pay-SHOH luh nü-may-roh dü sehr-VUHR]
context: 'Pécho' = verlan of 'choper' (to catch, get). Also used for flirting success.
'Être grave' = to be ridiculous, over the top (affectionate teasing).

front: Ça me saoule de faire la queue.
pronunciation: [sah muh SOOL duh fehr lah KUH]
context: 'Saouler' = to tire, annoy. Literally 'to make drunk'.
Slightly dated but still understood: 'de la balle' = great.
'Être une crème' = to be very kind.
'Se la péter' = to show off, act superior.

front: Il a pris la grosse tête depuis sa promotion.
pronunciation: [ee lah pree lah grohs TET duh-pwee sah proh-moh-SYOHN]
back: He's become big-headed since his promotion.
context: 'Prendre la grosse tête' = to become arrogant.

front: Faut pas pousser mémé dans les orties !
pronunciation: [foh pah poo-say may-MAY dahn lay zor-TEE]
context: Literally 'don't push grandma into the nettles'. Humorous: don't exaggerate.

front: Ces expressions sont à éviter en entretien d'embauche.
pronunciation: [say zek-spreh-syohn sohn tah ay-vee-tay ahn nahn-truh-tyan dahm-BOHSH]
back: These expressions should be avoided in a job interview.
context: Knowing slang means understanding people, and knowing when NOT to use it.
